messages.subject: Inline R code - Not recognized by Vim-R-plugin
messages.subject_clean: Inline R code - Not recognized by Vim-R-plugin
messages.body_plain:
HI,

I am using the vim-r-plugin (v1.1) for rmarkdown files. I've noticed that the vim-r-plugin does not seem to recognize Inline R Code:

```
There were `r nrow(cars)` cars studied
```

If I was to try to send this to the console, I would get the error:

> Not inside an R code chunk.

Is there a way to get the plugin to recognize these inline chunks?

Thanks,

Fong

messages.subject: Re: Inline R code - Not recognized by Vim-R-plugin
messages.subject_clean: Inline R code - Not recognized by Vim-R-plugin
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for asking the question!

It was possible to send inline code only with Rnoweb files, but I have just extended the feature to Rmd and Rrst too: https://github.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin/commit/d80fe50553fb908b505fcd53995b41b9e9f2e757

The new feature is available in the development version of the plugin, which I plan to release as stable on the next weekend.

messages.subject_clean: omnicompletion does not seem to work for objects
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for this wonderful plugin

I've set up everything according to the manual, and omni-completion works for R functions (C-X C-A) but not when I try to autocomplete object like a dataframe (using C-X C-O). The dataframe is viewable in the object browser, but when I type the dataframe with column name (like dfname$colu) and try to autocomplete, it returns 'pattern not found'.
Am i missing something?

Thanks in advance

Oren

messages.subject: Re: omnicompletion does not seem to work for objects
messages.subject_clean: omnicompletion does not seem to work for objects
messages.body_plain:
If you put in your ~/.Rprofile

options(vimcom.verbose = 4)

then, after <C-X><C-O>, you should get the an output similar to his in R:

VimCom Received: [8] homeuserdirfileRhOfK9sCv8Z7jGpdK5du8cgvimcom:::vim.bol("/tmp/r-plugin-user/GlobalEnvList_homeuserdirfileRhOfK9sCv8Z7jGpdK5du8cg")
vimcom_eval_expr: 'vimcom:::vim.bol("/tmp/r-plugin-user/GlobalEnvList_homeuserdirfileRhOfK9sCv8Z7jGpdK5du8cg")'

The first line is the message sent from Vim to R, and the second one is the command executed by R (the creation of the list of objects in R's workspace).

messages.body_plain:
To easily check what scripts Vim is reading at startup, you can start Vim in this way:

vim --startuptime /tmp/vimstttime script.R

Then, quit Vim and look at /tmp/vimstttime.
